section.controlled_paraphrase: When the referee judges that a stalemate has occurred or is likely, the referee proposes a rerack and break. If any player refuses, the referee permits play to continue for a period; generally each player receives three more shots, or the referee makes another judgment-based decision. If the stalemate remains, the referee declares it and reracks, with the original breaker breaking again and the original shooting order unchanged.

uniquely_determined_rules: the initial proposal is triggered by referee judgment, not by an automatic shot predicate
the proposal is to rerack and break
a refusal by any player causes play to continue for a referee-controlled period
after that continuation, a remaining stalemate requires a referee declaration before rerack
the final rerack assigns the break to the original breaking player
the original shooting order remains unchanged
text_does_not_uniquely_determine: a machine predicate for stalemate occurred or likely to occur
the signed referee identity and transport in each product mode
whether acceptance requires explicit responses from both players or an authority timeout
whether generally three more shots each is a default, recommendation, maximum, or replaceable allocation
the complete set of another judgment-based decisions
the ordering and accounting of the generally three shots when turns continue after legal pockets
which events prove that the stalemate was broken
the exact time at which the referee reassesses and issues the final declaration

row.assessment: No stalemate proposal/refusal state, three-shot counter or original-breaker rerack workflow exists.

why_implementation_is_blocked.referee_input: The rule delegates both the initial likelihood judgment and final declaration to a referee, but no signed referee authority or transport exists.
why_implementation_is_blocked.continuation_policy: The phrase generally three shots each expressly permits another referee decision and does not define a single fixed machine window.
why_implementation_is_blocked.state_identity: The current runtime does not retain a stable rack ID, original breaker or original shooting-order snapshot beyond transient break-decision offers.
why_implementation_is_blocked.counter_boundary: Replay and semantic-action shot counts are recording aids, not revision-bound per-player counters scoped to a referee continuation window.
why_implementation_is_blocked.rerack_boundary: Core E can execute a verified rerack for a caller-selected breaker, but without a Section 21 parent it cannot prove referee declaration, preserved order or correct reset.

count_only: one authoritative Shoot action accepted for the window's rack and current player
one shot whose rules lifecycle reaches an authoritative completed-shot boundary
never_count: aim, power, preview or placement input
a failed physics step or rolled-back shot
a replay seek, replay playback action or imported replay shot count
a shot from another rack, rules reset or superseded proposal

future_state_machine.proposal_transition: Validate signed referee input, rack identity, original breaker/order snapshot, policy version, authority revision/state hash and idempotency before publishing one blocking proposal.
future_state_machine.accept_transition: Only a policy-defined complete acceptance outcome may stage and atomically commit the original-breaker rerack; one player's acceptance may not bypass the other player's right to refuse.
future_state_machine.refusal_transition: Any valid player refusal closes response collection and activates exactly the signed referee continuation directive without rerack.
future_state_machine.progress_transition: Count only authoritative completed shots against the directive; reaching a numerical allowance never itself declares stalemate or reracks.
future_state_machine.final_transition: A fresh signed referee declaration bound to the same rack and completed directive stages one verified official rerack, restores the original breaker/order, then commits state, revision, event, action and receipt atomically.
future_state_machine.stalemate_broken_transition: Requires the future policy/referee input; it closes the subflow without rerack and resets its counters.

clear_all_stalemate_state_on: new rack or official rerack from another authority flow
reset_contract.superseded_proposal: A signed replacement may supersede only under a future policy; stale IDs remain rejected.

future_atomic_idempotency_contract.precommit: Validate ruleset, capability, rack/proposal/directive identity, actor class, player actor where applicable, exact action and payload, referee attestation, policy version, authority revision, state hash and idempotency before mutation.
future_atomic_idempotency_contract.rerack_staging: Build and verify the full Core E official rack plan for the frozen original breaker before the first parent mutation.
future_atomic_idempotency_contract.commit: Apply proposal, response, counter, closure or rerack plus one revision/event/action/receipt as one logical transaction.
future_atomic_idempotency_contract.original_breaker_and_order: The rerack breaker and order come only from the immutable rack-start snapshot, never from currentPlayer at proposal or declaration time.
future_atomic_idempotency_contract.failure_rollback: Runtime, rack, balls, current player, original order, counters, offers, receipts, authority revision/hash, events and journals remain byte-equivalent to pre-call state.
future_atomic_idempotency_contract.exact_retry: Returns the original ACK without a second proposal, response, count, declaration, rerack, revision, event or action.

forbidden_scope: production source edits in this design-gap task
hardcoding generally three shots each as mandatory policy
automatically detecting or finally declaring stalemate without referee input
using global replay shotCount as a rules-authoritative per-player continuation counter
inferring original breaker or order from currentPlayer at proposal time
calling the rack foundation directly as proof of a Section 21 parent transaction
exposing the pending stalemate UI or product seam
